candidates.description: A 4.5M-parameter two-voice English text-to-speech model, trained from scratch
candidates.readme_excerpt:
# tiny-voca

tiny-voca is a small English text-to-speech model. It has two voices, 4.5M
parameters, and runs on a CPU or in the browser.

[Demo](https://tiny-voca.n4ze3m.com) · [Weights](https://huggingface.co/n4ze3m/tiny-voca) · [Dataset](https://huggingface.co/datasets/n4ze3m/tiny-voca)

## Features

- **Small**: 4,537,291 parameters, 18 MB, waveform generator included.
- **Fast**: about 70x real time on four CPU threads.
- **Two voices**: F2 (female) and M2 (male), American English, 24 kHz.
- **Runs anywhere**: PyTorch, ONNX Runtime, and ONNX Runtime Web.
- **Open**: code, weights, training recipe and dataset. Trained from scratch.

## Install

```bash
git clone https://github.com/n4ze3m/tiny-voca.git
cd tiny-voca
pip install -e ".[own]"
hf download n4ze3m/tiny-voca --local-dir weights
export DIZIONE_DATA=weights/phonemizer
```

## Usage

```bash
python -m tiny_voca.infer \
  --checkpoint weights/tiny-voca.pt \
  --voice F2 \
  --text "Hello! This is tiny voca." \
  --output hello.wav
```

| Option | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `--text-file` | | Read the text from a file instead of `--text` |
| `--voice` | `F2` | `F2` or `M2` |
| `--speed` | 1.0 | Speaking rate |
| `--pitch-shift` | 0 | Raise or lower the pitch |
| `--pitch-range` | 1.0 | More or less pitch movement |

Long text is fine. It is read one sentence at a time and the audio is joined.
A text that ends without a mark gets a full stop, so the last word does not
break off. A sentence with nothing to read, such as one in another script, is
skipped. The output never peaks above 0.99, so it does not clip as a 16-bit
WAV. In Python, `tiny_voca.infer.speak_text` does the same.

## ONNX

```bash
python -m tiny_voca.export --checkpoint weights/tiny-voca.pt --output tiny-voca.onnx
```

A ready file is in the weights repository as `onnx/model.onnx`. The
[model card](https://huggingface.co/n4ze3m/tiny-voca) shows how to call it.

## Web demo

The [demo](https://tiny-voca.n4ze3m.com) runs the model in the browser. It
plays each sentence as soon as it is made, and keeps the whole clip in the
player. Its source is in `web/`.

```bash
cd web
bash fetch_assets.sh /path/to/dizione
npx wrangler dev
```

## Training

```bash
export TINY_VOCA_FRONTEND=own
python -m tiny_voca.prepare --inputs data/train-*.parquet --split train --output features
python -m tiny_voca.annotate --features features --output annotations
python -m tiny_voca.train --train annotations/train.jsonl --validation annotations/validation.j

# Jev-Interaction **System-One-controlled full-duplex voice interaction.**
Turn-taking as decisions you write — not a model you train. [中文](README.zh-CN.md) · [Profiles](jev_interaction/profiles) · [Decisions](jev_interaction/judge/questions.py) [![tests](https://github.com/native-bond-lab/Jev-Interaction/actions/workflows/tests.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/native-bond-lab/Jev-Interaction/actions/workflows/tests.yml) ![python](https://img.shields.io/badge/python-3.10%2B-3776ab) ![license](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-Apache--2.0-blue) ![status](https://img.shields.io/badge/status-alpha-f59e0b) ![judge](https://img.shields.io/badge/judge-Jev-0f766e) ![duplex](https://img.shields.io/badge/full--duplex-voice-6366f1)
*Most of a conversation happens in the gaps: who waits, who yields, who answers with nothing but an "mm-hm".
We wrote every gap down as a question, and gave the questions to Jev.* Try it here: [Try it now](https://pupunpu-jev-interaction.hf.space/).
> **Built on [Jev](https://typesafe.ai).** Every turn-taking decision here is a question Jev answers in tens of > milliseconds. Without it, none of this would work. ![Jev-Interaction architecture](docs/architecture.svg) **Full duplex from a cascade.** Speech recognition → Jev's decisions → any language model → any speech synthesis. The agent listens while it talks, says "mm-hm" while you talk, lets a pause stand, carries on through a backchannel, yields or finishes its sentence when you cut in, and picks the call back up after a silence. **A System One for conversation.** People on a call run two minds at once: a fast one that knows, without thinking, when to wait, when to yield and when to say "mm-hm", and a slow one that works out what to say. Here Jev is the fast mind, deciding each moment in tens of milliseconds; the language model is the slow one, writing the words. Neither waits for the other. Voice agents today take one of two roads. **Cascades** bolt a small trained model onto that pipeline to guess *"has the user finished?"* and leave everything else to timers. **End-to-end full-duplex models** (Moshi, GPT-4o Realtime, Gemini Live) learn turn-taking inside one large speech model: fast and natural, but a black box. # Open Generative Search Optimization (OpenGSO)

> **Early release.** Until 1.0, a minor release may change a command, a flag, a config field or an export.

Make your website readable by AI agents: score it, write a markdown twin of every page, and serve
the twin at the same URL whenever an agent asks for it. Any framework or static host. No headless
browser, no account, no telemetry.

[![npm](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/opengso)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/opengso)
[![Checks](https://github.com/sherwinvishesh/OpenGSO/actions/workflows/checks.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/sherwinvishesh/OpenGSO/actions/workflows/checks.yml)
[![node](https://img.shields.io/node/v/opengso)](https://nodejs.org)
[![license](https://img.shields.io/npm/l/opengso)](LICENSE)

![opengso test, generate and test again on the bundled Next.js demo. The first test scores 65 of 100 with no robots.txt, no sitemap.xml and no markdown twin. Generate writes three twins and the three root files in 126 milliseconds. The second test scores 100 of 100 with 14 of 15 suggestions adopted.](docs/images/demo.svg)

That is the whole loop, as the CLI printed it against the bundled demo: a Next.js site with no
`robots.txt`, no `sitemap.xml` and no twins scores **65**, `opengso generate` writes six files in
126 ms, and the same URL scores **100** with 14 of 15 suggestions adopted. Every character is
captured output; `scripts/render-recording.mjs` turns the captures into the animation.

ChatGPT, Claude, Perplexity and the crawlers behind them fetch pages the way `curl` does: no
JavaScript runs, and every byte of markup costs tokens. OpenGSO is three commands. **test** scores
what an agent receives, 0 to 100, with the reason for every point. **generate** writes a markdown
twin of every page, plus `robots.txt`, `llms.txt` and `sitemap.xml`. **prod** is a zero-dependency
middleware that serves the twin to agents and the page to people, at the same URL, without a
redirect.

## Ten seconds: what an agent gets

`GET /resume` on the bundled demo, as ChatGPT or Claude receives it **today**. 13,671 bytes, of
which 10,333 sit inside ten `<script>` tags, and the article is sent twice: once as HTML and once
again inside the framework's payload. Long lines are cut where marked.

<script src="/_next/static/chunks/19mx3mg6lkumu.js" async=""></script>
<script src="/_next/stati

## Agent Presence

Real conversation should not leave you waiting after a single sentence, nor
should it grind to a halt just because the Agent is looking something up,
calling a tool, or working on a task.

Conversation should keep flowing, and the Agent should always be present.

That is why we built **qwen-audio-agent**—a realtime voice runtime that keeps
Agents talking, working, and present. Whether chatting with you, thinking
through a problem, or working on a task, your Agent remains in the
conversation. It listens, responds, and when the task is complete, naturally
tells you:

"It's ready."

candidates.description: Playwright MCP server
candidates.readme_excerpt:
## Playwright MCP A Model Context Protocol (MCP) server that provides browser automation capabilities using [Playwright](https://playwright.dev). This server enables LLMs to interact with web pages through structured accessibility snapshots, bypassing the need for screenshots or visually-tuned models. ### Playwright MCP vs Playwright CLI This package provides MCP interface into Playwright. If you are using a **coding agent**, you might benefit from using the [CLI+SKILLS](https://github.com/microsoft/playwright-cli) instead. - **CLI**: Modern **coding agents** increasingly favor CLI–based workflows exposed as SKILLs over MCP because CLI invocations are more token-efficient: they avoid loading large tool schemas and verbose accessibility trees into the model context, allowing agents to act through concise, purpose-built commands. This makes CLI + SKILLs better suited for high-throughput coding agents that must balance browser automation with large codebases, tests, and reasoning within limited context windows.
**Learn more about [Playwright CLI with SKILLS](https://github.com/microsoft/playwright-cli)**. - **MCP**: MCP remains relevant for specialized agentic loops that benefit from persistent state, rich introspection, and iterative reasoning over page structure, such as exploratory automation, self-healing tests, or long-running autonomous workflows where maintaining continuous browser context outweighs token cost concerns. ### Key Features - **Fast and lightweight**. Uses Playwright's accessibility tree, not pixel-based input. - **LLM-friendly**. No vision models needed, operates purely on structured data. - **Deterministic tool application**. Avoids ambiguity common with screenshot-based approaches. ### Requirements - Node.js 18 or newer - VS Code, Cursor, Windsurf, Claude Desktop, Goose, Grok, Junie or any other MCP client ### Getting started First, install the Playwright MCP server with your client. **Standard config** works in most of the tools: ```js { "mcpServers": { "playwright": { "command": "npx", "args": [ "@playwright/mcp@latest" ] } } } ``` [](https://insiders.vscode.dev/redirect?url=vscode%3Amcp%2Finstall%3F%257B%2522name%2522%253A%2522playwright%2522%252C%2522command%2522%253A%2522npx%2522%252C%2522

# gstack

gstack turns Claude Code (and other coding agents) into a virtual engineering team: a CEO who rethinks the product, an eng manager who locks architecture, a designer who catches AI slop, a reviewer who finds production bugs, a QA lead who opens a real browser, a security officer who runs OWASP + STRIDE audits, and a release engineer who ships the PR. All slash commands, all Markdown, all free, MIT license.

I'm [Garry Tan](https://x.com/garrytan), President & CEO of [Y Combinator](https://www.ycombinator.com/). This is the open source software factory I use every day, and I'm sharing it because these tools should be available to everyone. The story, the productivity numbers and how I run ten sprints at once are in [Why gstack](docs/why-gstack.md).

Fork it. Improve it. Make it yours. And if you want to hate on free open source software — you're welcome to, but I'd rather you just try it first.

**Who this is for:**
- **Founders and CEOs** — especially technical ones who still want to ship
- **First-time Claude Code users** — structured roles instead of a blank prompt
- **Tech leads and staff engineers** — rigorous review, QA, and release automation on every PR

## What gstack is for

- **A whole team's judgment for one builder.** Product, design, engineering, QA, security and release reviews, each from a specialist role.
- **Catch what CI misses.** Find the bugs that pass tests but break in production, before they ship.
- **AI-written changes you can trust.** Every change carries its tests, its review and the evidence for both, so you can merge without rereading every line.
- **Free, open and portable.** MIT-licensed, and it runs on Claude Code and the other major coding agents.

## Quick start

1. Install gstack (two pastes, about 30 seconds of setup; see below).
2. Run `/office-hours` and describe what you're building. It pushes back on your framing and writes a design doc the other skills read.
3. Run `/review` on any branch with changes. It finds the bugs that pass CI but break in production, and fixes the obvious ones.
4. Run `/qa` on your staging URL, or on an isolated local API, CLI, job or webhook. It opens a real browser, reproduces bugs and fixes them.

Stop there. You'll know if this is for you. When you want the whole sprint, `/autoplan` reviews a plan end to end and `/ship` runs tests, review and the PR.

candidates.readme_excerpt:
# agent-browser Browser automation for AI agents: open pages, read them as an accessibility tree, and act on elements from the shell.

agent-browser is a native Rust CLI that gives an AI agent a browser it can drive one command at a time. `snapshot` returns the page as compact text with a ref such as `@e1` for each element. The agent acts on a ref, reads the page again to check the result, and repeats. The browser stays open between commands, so each step is one short shell call. ## Install ```bash npm install -g agent-browser agent-browser install # download Chrome for Testing (first time only) ``` - **Homebrew:** `brew install agent-browser`, then `agent-browser install`. - **Linux:** `agent-browser install --with-deps` also installs the browser's system libraries. - **No install:** `npx agent-browser open example.com`. Project installs, building from source, `upgrade`, and `doctor` are covered in [Installation](https://agent-browser.dev/installation). ## Quick start ```bash agent-browser open example.com agent-browser snapshot -i # interactive elements, each with a ref agent-browser click @e1 # act on a ref from that snapshot agent-browser get url # check the result agent-browser close ``` The snapshot for `example.com`: ``` - link "Learn more" [ref=e1] ``` - Refs describe the page at the time of the snapshot.
